title: Paraeus and Baron: habitual faith in mortal fallers does not justify
source_text: XXXIX. Nec enim possunt Renati, quum in peccatis contra conscientiam perseverant, amittere veram fidem, quin fides eorum separetur a Dei & proximi dilectione, & sic desinat esse vera, id est, salvifica atque justificans, quia cessat ab actu salvandi & justificandi, neque talis est, ut Deo hominem gratum & acceptum reddat. Quod etiam conforme est sententiae Davidis Paraei; Fides, inquit, in lapsis habitualiter tantum manens, proprie justificans dici, aut eos justificare non potest. In lib. 1. Bellarm. de Amissione Gratiae, cap. 7. sub finem. Quod probans Rob. Baronius, dicit Fidem, quoad actum illum vivum, quo justificat, in renatis mortaliter peccantibus interrumpi, & deliquium pati; ita ut durante eo statu, eos justificare, aut fides justificans dici non possit. Disput. de Peccato mortali & veniali, sect. 1. num. 5.
pass_a_gloss: For the regenerate, when they persevere in sins against conscience, cannot lose true faith without their faith being separated from love of God and neighbor, and so ceasing to be true — that is, saving and justifying — because it ceases from the act of saving and justifying, and is not such as to render the man pleasing and acceptable to God. Which also conforms to David Paraeus's opinion: Faith, he says, remaining in the fallen only habitually cannot properly be called justifying, or justify them (on Bellarmine On the Loss of Grace book 1 ch. 7 toward the end). Which Robert Baron proving says: Faith, as to that living act by which it justifies, is interrupted in the regenerate who sin mortally, and suffers a faint; so that while that state lasts it cannot justify them, or be called justifying faith (Disputation on Mortal and Venial Sin, sect. 1 n. 5).
pass_b_english: Losing true faith in known sin means separation from love — faith ceases saving/justifying.
Paraeus and Baron: habitual-only faith in mortal fallers is interrupted and does not justify for that time.

choices.why: Justifying act interrupted, habit may remain.
